column1: # The TypeScript evaluation corpus — the DEFINITION, not a description of one.
# Why this file exists: every held-out figure ever quoted for this front end came from
# a corpus that lived in /tmp and a dev/holdout split that lived in an agent's head.
# `git grep held-out` on main returned nothing. So no rate was reproducible, and a
# corpus member could stop producing ground truth without anyone noticing — which is
# what issue #143 found, and what a full run at the current head confirms: SEVEN of the
# nine projects below cannot be measured at all, and the two sets between them were
# reporting on subtrees nobody chose.
#   name  set  path  repo  commit  note
# `note` is the last field and may contain spaces. `path` is relative to the clone;
# `.` means the repository root IS the project.
# dev      designed against. A rule may be derived from what these projects show.
# holdout  DESIGN-BLIND. Measured, never used to derive a rule. When it surfaces a
#          defect class, the shape is reproduced SYNTHETICALLY under cases/ and the
#          rule designed from that — never from the held-out site itself.
#          A change that closes the dev/holdout gap is suspicious, not good: that gap
#          IS the generalisation cost.
# blocked  IN THE CORPUS AND NOT MEASURABLE. Kept here, with the reason, because a
#          manifest that silently drops what it cannot measure is how a held-out set
#          came to be three projects none of which worked. Each carries the issue that
#          would return it to service. run-corpus.sh skips these.
# ── PATH: why package level, not repository root (issue #143) ────────────────
# On a workspace repository the IR carries `filePath` relative to each package with no
# package qualifier, so two packages' `src/index.ts` collide on one key and nothing
# joins (parser#70). The parser handles a SINGLE package correctly, so a workspace repo
# is entered at its principal published package. But package-level entry has its own
# cost, visible in the blocked rows: the harness mirrors the project directory, and a
# package tsconfig that `extends` or `references` ABOVE its own root loses the target.
# $TS_CORPUS, defaulting to ~/.cache/axiom-ts-corpus. Deliberately NOT /tmp: the corpus
# was kept there and the system reaper removed every source file from all nine projects
# mid-session — directories and node_modules left standing, .git gone — which surfaced
# as four harness failures that looked like four unrelated bugs. fetch.sh reclones at the
# pinned commits, which is the only reason that was recoverable.
# run-corpus.sh sets SCORE_PRODUCTION=1. A repository's test tree is routinely larger
# than the library it tests — typeorm 70,534 test sites against 17,062 production, and
# its conservation loss is 11.58% over the former and 0.04% over the latter. Unfiltered,
# that project reads as 9.3% lost and gets discarded; filtered, it is the only sound
# held-out project there is.
# ── name      set      path                   repo                                        commit   note
immer         dev      .                      https://github.com/immerjs/immer.git         061c242  566 production sites, 0.00% loss

remeda        dev      packages/remeda        https://github.com/remeda/remeda.git         e11dcf2  652 production sites, 0.00% loss. Was recorded as 11,818 until #280: 23,011 sites analysed, and the production filter matched `.test.ts` but not the `.test-d.ts` type-test convention, so 11,055 of that 11,818 were type tests. They score far better than real code — an expectTypeOf chain is about as easy as a call site gets — so the leak RAISED the development rate rather than diluting it. The 652 is the real figure and this is now the SMALLEST dev member, not the largest
zustand       dev      .                      https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand.git        b57db4f  218 production sites, 0.00% loss (3.54% loss over its test tree alone)

trpc          dev      packages/server        https://github.com/trpc/trpc.git             6a70335  3,048 production sites, 0% loss, 0 diagnostics. Was oracle-refused at 1791/3023 with 658 diagnostics until the mirror carried its extends chain (#240); its tsconfig extends ../../tsconfig.json. Exact 0.577, below the other dev members - it is a harder project, not a broken one

typeorm       holdout  .                      https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm.git       b495ed4  17,062 production sites, 0.04% loss. Larger than the whole dev set, which is what makes it a real check

axios         blocked  .                      https://github.com/axios/axios.git           fede1d1  NOT A TYPESCRIPT PROJECT. 192 .js files; the only .ts are index.d.ts and deno/bun smoke tests. Oracle resolved 348/1139 with 103 diagnostics. Remove rather than fix

nest          blocked  packages/core          https://github.com/nestjs/nest.git           1eeccd3  NOT the extends chain - #240 mirrors its ../tsconfig.build.json correctly and it is present in the mirror. The oracle still builds an EMPTY program (0 sites, 0 diagnostics) because packages/core/tsconfig.json is solution-style: files:[] include:[] references:[./tsconfig.build.json], so parseJsonConfigFileContent yields no file names and the oracle does not follow references. At the repository root instead it joins 6800 of 10005 oracle sites - 32% conservation loss, the parser#70 filePath collision. Unmeasurable at either path until one of those two is fixed

vue-core      blocked  packages/runtime-core  https://github.com/vuejs/core.git            d63616c  No tsconfig.json in the package at all; the governing one is at the repo root, outside the mirror. Oracle: "no tsconfig.json under <mirror>"

rxjs          blocked  packages/rxjs          https://github.com/ReactiveX/rxjs.git        54796b3  Oracle refused: 20056/69451 resolved, 25996 diagnostics. Its own tsconfig is not the build config — 20,154 diagnostics are implicit-any from spec helpers and 1,993 are "Observable only refers to a type"
